subject: Derivative routing & subprocessor onboarding — limited model adaptation ask
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@medsentry.com>
To: david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsentry.com
Date: Sun, 14 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — dataflow and adaptation limits

Hi David,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. Two follow-ups from our security and procurement teams:

1) We need a clear inventory of subprocessors that will touch ML inference request/response payloads (including logging, telemetry, and persistent caches). Can you attach a CSV or spreadsheet with names, countries, and purpose?

2) We require a contractual commitment that MedSentry's customer interactions will not be used to further train or adapt any public or shared model. We know Redwood has model variants — if you can describe the operational guardrails (routing, model pinning, and fallback behavior) that prevent adaptive training, that will help legal sign-off.

Ideally procurement would like to see a DPA redline with a concrete "no adaptive training" clause and an ops diagram showing where ephemeral caches are used vs. durable logs.

Can you send those items this week?

Thanks — Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Security, MedSentry Health
samira.k@medsentry.com

From: david_kim@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@medsentry.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — dataflow and adaptation limits

Hi Samira — appreciate the clear list. Attaching the subprocessor inventory and a draft DPA that includes a no-adaptive-training commitment. High level notes below; the attachments have the details you asked for.

Summary of operational guarantees:
- No adaptive training: Redwood will not include MedSentry tenant data in any model training or tuning pipeline. The DPA draft includes a one-line commitment plus an appendix describing evidence paths.
- Model pinning & routing: Customer requests are pinned to the customer-selected model variant; we have routing policies that prevent automated promotion of traffic to training buckets.
- Cache handling: Ephemeral KV caches are used in-memory on serving nodes and are scoped per customer; persistent logs (request/response traces) are retained only where agreed and are redacted by default.
- Subprocessors: The attached inventory lists all current subprocessors that may access stored traces for troubleshooting. Any subprocessors that touch raw customer payloads are flagged.

Next steps we propose:
1) Kimberly (legal ops) and Jordan (platform ops) and I will review your redline and provide an annotated DPA by EOD Thursday.
2) We can run a short technical call to walk through the dataflow_diagram.png and demonstrate how route policies and pinning work (15–20 min).

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv; dataflow_diagram.png; dpa_draft.pdf

Best,
David Kim
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: dav id_kim@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: FW: onboarding questions — MedSentry 

Kimberly / Jordan — forwarding Samira's ask and my draft. Key asks from MedSentry: full subprocessor table (we have one but need to mark "touches raw payload"), an explicit no-adaptive-training clause in the DPA, and a simple ops diagram for routing/pinning.

Action items: 
- Kimberly: can you drive a DPA redline that includes an operational evidence appendix (they want a one-page ops proof + list of how to request evidence)? Suggest we include: log retention buckets, redaction policy, and proof of no training path (e.g., config screenshots + runbook excerpt).
- Jordan: please confirm which subprocessors currently have access to persistent traces versus ephemeral caches and flag any that would require approval for escrow or onshore routing. If you can add a column in the attached CSV ("raw_payload_access: yes/no"), that will help procurement.

Target: consolidated reply to MedSentry with attachments and 15-minute technical walkthrough options by EOD today (we committed to a quick turnaround).

Thanks — David

[This internal note was short and action-oriented; replies expected inline.]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@medsentry.com>, david_kim@redwood.com
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: onboarding questions — dataflow and adaptation limits

Hi Samira — thanks for the clear asks, and David/Jordan thanks for the quick turnaround. Please find attached the items you requested. Highlights: 

- DPA redline: Section 6.3 (Data Use for Model Development) now includes: "Redwood shall not use Customer data to train, fine-tune, or adapt any model not expressly dedicated and isolated for that Customer, except with Customer's prior written consent." We added an appendix (Appendix B) that lists the evidence items and the request flow (how to request logs, redaction proofs, or onshore transfer).

- Subprocessor inventory: CSV column "raw_payload_access" set to YES for three internal analytics partners that handle anonymized traces for billing and performance. None of the public model training vendors have access.

- Dataflow diagram: shows request path, ephemeral KV caches (in green), and persistent trace stores (in red). The diagram notes that ephemeral caches never leave the serving cluster and are evicted within 60s for interactive sessions.

Next steps: 
1) If procurement wants further guarantees (e.g., SFTP-only export lanes or KMS-onshore for their tenant), we can scope that as an addendum.
2) Jordan will join the technical call to demo routing/pinning.

Samira — are you available Tues or Wed morning Pacific for a 20-minute ops walkthrough?

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Contracts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv; dataflow_diagram.png; dpa_draft_redline.pdf
